tldr_label: TL;DR — Israel's election ends in deadlock; chip stocks surge in Seoul as the Fed and Big Tech report today

tldr_bullets.label: Israel
tldr_bullets.body: With most votes counted, the Times of Israel reported Netanyahu's bloc at 54 seats, Eisenkot's at 47 and Arab parties at 19. No bloc has the 61 needed, and both leaders claim victory. [[TAG:warning:no majority]]

tldr_bullets.label: Iran
tldr_bullets.body: Mojtaba Khamenei said Iran's state of 'neither war nor peace' must end. Trump said he is weighing a deal against action to 'finish them off'.

tldr_bullets.label: Markets
tldr_bullets.body: Seoul's Kospi jumped more than 6% to above 6,000 after SK Hynix posted record profit. Wall Street awaits the Fed at 2 p.m. ET and results from Microsoft and Alphabet. [[TAG:success:Kospi +6.6%]]

tldr_bullets.label: Ukraine
tldr_bullets.body: The Oleshky truce has spread across Kherson region with no reported breaches. Finland and Norway's call with Putin split the Nordic countries.

tldr_bullets.label: Middle East
tldr_bullets.body: The Houthis called Egypt's authorization of military support for Saudi Arabia a 'declaration of war'.

sections.title: Israel Deadlocked
sections.summary: Neither bloc reaches 61 seats; Arab parties hold the balance and both leaders claim victory

paragraphs.heading: The count
paragraphs.body: Citing Central Elections Committee figures with about three-quarters of ballots counted, the Times of Israel reported 54 seats for Netanyahu's Likud-led bloc, 47 for the bloc led by Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot, and 19 for the two Arab-led parties. Ynet had earlier put Netanyahu's bloc at 55 with about half the vote counted. Exit polls varied. Al Jazeera reported no clear winner, and Axios described the blocs as deadlocked. Soldiers' and special ballots could still move the numbers. [[TAG:warning:count ongoing]]

paragraphs.heading: Paths to power
paragraphs.body: Eisenkot declared victory and argued that he should get the first chance to form a government, Al Jazeera reported. Netanyahu also claimed victory and said Israel must not form a government that relies on 'anti-Zionist Arab parties'. Both leaders ruled out partnering with the Arab parties during the campaign. Analysts cited by SBS and Al Jazeera see a unity government or another election as more likely than a minority government. [[TAG:info:repeat vote possible]]

paragraphs.heading: Market reaction
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Israeli bonds and the shekel fell as investors priced in a long stalemate.

sections.title: Iran Standoff
sections.summary: Khamenei wants 'neither war nor peace' to end as Trump weighs a deal against new strikes

paragraphs.heading: Tehran's terms
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei met security chief Mohsen Rezaei on Tuesday to discuss Iran's conditions for ending the war. Khamenei said the state of 'neither war nor peace' must end and stressed continued control over the Strait of Hormuz. Oil prices eased after the meeting.

paragraphs.heading: Washington's options
paragraphs.body: CBS reported that Trump said he is weighing a deal with Iran against action to 'finish them off'. Talks have looked stalled for weeks, but Iran says messages are still passing to the US. CBS also reported Iranian missile and drone fire toward Jordan and Bahrain in recent days. [[TAG:danger:strikes possible]]

sections.title: Red Sea Front
sections.summary: Houthis call Egypt's authorization of military support for Saudi Arabia a declaration of war

paragraphs.heading: Cairo's vote
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and US News reported that on October 26 Egypt's parliament authorized President Sisi to take 'all necessary measures' to help Saudi Arabia defend itself against Houthi attacks. The Jerusalem Post said Riyadh has not yet made a formal request. Officials say any Egyptian troops would stay on Saudi soil and would not join strikes in Yemen.

paragraphs.heading: Houthi warning
paragraphs.body: Israel Hayom reported that Houthi politburo member Mohammed Ali al-Houthi called the move tantamount to a declaration of war. The vote follows near-daily Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia since early October. Troop numbers and the form of support have not been disclosed. [[TAG:warning:escalation risk]]

sections.title: Ukraine and Europe
sections.summary: Oleshky truce widens across Kherson; Nordic call with Putin exposes a European rift

paragraphs.heading: Kherson truce
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera reported that Russia paused strikes on Kherson when a local truce took effect on Tuesday, ahead of a humanitarian mission led by Melania Trump. CNN and the Kyiv Independent said she announced the ceasefire had expanded within Kherson Oblast. Ukraine said there were no breaches in the first 30 hours, LBC reported. The deal covers demining, aid deliveries and evacuations from Oleshky, where up to 2,000 people remain. [[TAG:success:truce holding]]

paragraphs.heading: Nordic split
paragraphs.body: NBC News reported that Finland's Alexander Stubb and Norway's Jonas Gahr Støre held a rare call with Putin and urged a restart of peace talks. Euronews reported that Denmark's Mette Frederiksen criticized the call as uncoordinated, while Sweden's Ulf Kristersson warned against splitting Europe's voice.

sections.title: Markets and the Fed
sections.summary: Kospi tops 6,000 on SK Hynix results; Fed, Microsoft and Alphabet are due today

paragraphs.heading: Seoul surges
paragraphs.body: Korea JoongAng Daily reported that the Kospi rose 6.63% to 6,012.44 after SK Hynix posted record third-quarter operating profit of 83.33 trillion won. AP, via ABC4, put the close at 6,023.73, up 6.8%, so sources differ slightly on the final figure. SK Hynix shares rose about 11%, CoinDesk reported. [[TAG:success:Kospi above 6,000]]

paragraphs.heading: Wall Street
paragraphs.body: CNBC reported that on Tuesday the S&P 500 rose about 0.6% to 7,722.60, the Nasdaq gained about 1.2% to 26,477.81, and the Dow was nearly flat at 52,377.57. Yahoo Finance said chipmakers led the gains. Prices for oil vary by source and timing: Voice of Emirates reported a Brent settlement of $115.15, while FXEmpire said prices eased on hopes of peace with Iran.

paragraphs.heading: Fed and Big Tech
paragraphs.body: CNBC said futures put the chance of a hold at about 90%, at 3.75% to 4.00%, with the decision due at 2 p.m. ET followed by Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference. EBC reported that markets expect a hike in December. Saxo said Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close, with investors focused on whether AI spending is paying off. [[TAG:info:Fed 2 p.m. ET]]

sections.title: US Midterms
sections.summary: Six days out, Democrats lead the generic ballot as Trump's approval sits near record lows

paragraphs.heading: The polls
paragraphs.body: A Marist poll of registered voters taken October 19 to 20 found Democrats leading the generic congressional ballot by 8 points, with Trump's approval at 40% among likely voters. Yahoo News, citing a New York Times average, put his approval at 37%. PBS NewsHour said disapproval of Trump is driving early turnout. Figures vary by pollster and by whether they survey likely or registered voters. [[TAG:info:vote Nov 3]]

sections.title: Africa and Health
sections.summary: Ebola passes 10,000 cases in DR Congo; dozens of Orthodox Christians killed in Oromia

paragraphs.heading: Ebola
paragraphs.body: Al Jazeera and CBC reported that confirmed Ebola cases in DR Congo have passed 10,000, with 4,887 deaths. Officials call it the country's fastest-growing outbreak on record. It is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, which has no approved vaccine. [[TAG:danger:4,887 deaths]]

paragraphs.heading: Ethiopia
paragraphs.body: The Ethiopian Orthodox Church said at least 60 Christians were killed in two attacks in Oromia's Arsi Zone, ABC News and Al Jazeera reported. AFP, via CTV, cited residents and ACLED putting one attack's toll at at least 43. The regional government blamed the Oromo Liberation Army without presenting evidence, and no group has claimed responsibility. [[TAG:warning:toll disputed]]

paragraphs.heading: Gaza
paragraphs.body: CBC reported that a UN commission found Israel has continued to commit genocide in Gaza since the truce. Israel has dismissed the findings.
